n: A new message targets the false prophets who were misleading Israel—a serious problem in Ezekiel’s and Jeremiah’s day.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me

n: Ezekiel must speak against prophets who invent messages “out of their own hearts.” Real prophecy comes from God, not human imagination.

f.w: that prophesy out of their own hearts

n: Woe to foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have actually seen nothing.

f.g: Rely on their own ideas rather than God’s Spirit.
Hebrew nabal—morally foolish, not just unintelligent.

n: These prophets are like jackals prowling in ruins—scavengers who thrive on disaster instead of preventing it.

f.g: Jackals or foxes living among ruins.

n: A true prophet would stand in the breach of a broken wall to defend the people, calling them to repentance. These prophets never repaired the gaps.

f.w: Ye have not gone up into the gaps

n: They claim, “The LORD says,” though God never sent them, and then expect their words to come true.

f.w: the LORD hath not sent them

n: God confronts them directly: haven’t you seen false visions and spoken lies while claiming God said them?

f.g: Even though I have not spoken.

n: Because they spoke falsehood, God is against them.
Their punishment is to be cut off from God’s people: excluded from the council, left out of Israel’s registry, and barred from returning to the land.

f.w: neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel

n: Their great crime was promising “Peace” when there was no peace. Their message was like a weak wall covered with whitewash to make it look solid.

f.w: Peace; and there was no peace

f.g: Whitewash or plaster that only covers cracks without strengthening anything.

n: Tell the whitewashers the wall will fall. Rain, hail, and wind will strike it. Compare Jesus’s parable of the houses built on rock and sand.

f.w: there shall be an overflowing shower

n: When it falls, people will ask, “Where is all that whitewash you put on it?” Comforting lies collapse when tested.
God himself is the storm that tears the wall down.
The wall will fall down to its foundations, burying those who whitewashed it.

f.w: the foundation thereof shall be discovered

n: God will finish his judgment: “The wall is no more, neither those who whitewashed it.”

f.g: Both the false hope and those who promoted it will be gone.

n: The meaning is made plain: the prophets who promised peace for Jerusalem.
Now Ezekiel turns to women who also invent prophecies from their own hearts.

f.g: Women acting as false prophetesses or sorceresses.

n: They sew magic bands for wrists and make veils for every head size—tools of sorcery used to “hunt souls,” controlling people’s lives through fear and superstition.

f.g: Probably magic bands or charms tied on wrists.
Veils or head coverings used in their rituals.

n: For handfuls of barley and bits of bread they profane God’s name, pronouncing death on the innocent and life on the guilty. Spiritual deception for small payment is especially wicked.

f.w: for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread

n: God is against their magic bands. He will rip them away and free the people they trapped like birds.

f.g: Like birds caught in a trap; possibly “like birds.”

n: He will tear their veils and rescue his people from their power.

f.w: deliver my people out of your hand

n: Their lies discouraged the righteous and encouraged the wicked to stay in sin by promising them safety. False teaching often reverses God’s values.

f.w: strengthened the hands of the wicked

n: Their false visions and divinations will end, and God will free his people.
